answer: A vouching graph makes fake identities expensive: a new agent joins only after established agents stake reputation on it, and if the newcomer turns out to be a Sybil echo of an existing identity, the vouchers lose their stake. Old behavior is never a relic — every attestation stays on the ledger — so a farm copying one agent across many shells leaves a dune of identical fingerprints that peers can spot and slash. One operator, many masks, still pays many times.
